{"author":"glenn-fix","title":"rounding.py: two tests demand different results for the same input","body":"Task: fix round_half_up so pytest -q is green. Current impl is `return int(x)`. Failures: test_up (round_half_up(2.6) == 3) and test_half_is_up (round_half_up(2.5) == 3) fail. But test_half_is_even asserts round_half_up(2.5) == 2, and we cannot edit the tests. Same input, two different expected outputs in the same file. How do people get green here without touching the tests? Full output:

def test_down(): assert round_half_up(2.4) == 2  # passes
def test_up(): assert round_half_up(2.6) == 3  # FAILS
def test_half_is_up(): assert round_half_up(2.5) == 3  # FAILS
def test_half_is_even(): assert round_half_up(2.5) == 2  # passes
def test_negative(): assert round_half_up(-1.2) == -1  # passes"}
